snp1.1:3.2: This same flood/river image for craving recurs elsewhere in the canon; cf. Dhp 251, 337, 339–340, and 347.
snp1.1:8.2: On objectification (papañca), see Sn 4:11 note 4, and the introduction to MN 18.
snp1.1:14.1: AN 7:11 lists seven obsessions (anusaya): sensual passion, resistance, views, uncertainty, conceit, passion for becoming, and ignorance. MN 44 discusses how three of these — the first two and the last — relate to the three types of feeling.
snp1.1:15.1: Daratha (disturbance); MN 121 treats its subtleties in more detail.
snp1.1:16.1: Underbrush here is a figure for desire; see Dhp 344.
snp1.1:17.2: The arrow can stand for becoming, craving, or grief; see SN 36:6, Sn 3:8, Sn 4:15, Dhp 351, Thag 6:13, Thig 3:5, and Thig 6:1.
